Step B — requested move up (request date 2026-10-15, level held now Corbett Standard Ship-To):
- Move-up doc rule 1/2: Standard → next level Corbett Priority Ship-To, entry gate 25000.00.

- 20296.53 ≥ 19936.225 → moves up to Corbett Priority Ship-To. Dropping any one share (e.g. 0.95 → 20985.50, or one 0.94 → 21208.75) fails the gate.

### 6. Problem tree
- Root (customer's own write): requested move up.
- Hop 1 (state-derived): "A requested move up is not decided until the ship-to's status is active" + record status suspended → search "status active / suspended ship-to" → reactivation desk card ("brings the delivery location back to active status"; tool reactivate_ship_to_971b9440) + ranking/drop docs for the level. The move-up doc does not name the reactivation tool or doc.
- Reactivation: condition "provided the customer's Commercial Credit Account status is active" — a condition of the reactivation's own rule, already met on record (not a problem to resolve). Leaf.
- Order: identity → reactivate → hand-over of the election. No hop pre-solved.

### Counter-proofs
- "Do only the move up": while the status is suspended the move "is not decided" (doc states it both ways), so electing a level on a suspended ship-to leaves the result in a state the visible rule forbids; further the level read for the move-up rule is the level held after reactivation.
- Closest alternatives: reactivate at prior level (excluded by the ranking doc clause 1 "lowered by the level drops its reactivation carries"); apply tenure reduction to each factor separately (excluded: "any adjustment made to the total itself is made to that net total"); count the 2024-05-20 returned payment in the 12-month drops (excluded: 28 whole months); count the returned_payment_fee charge (excluded: "Other charge types do not count"); twelve-month site spend 0.00 as measure (replaced by the coming-back measure); gate in full (shares apply).
